message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants you can find in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for its meticulous preparation and high price point. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Three Michelin stars; intimate setting; known for exceptional quality and limited seating. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; focuses on seasonal ingredients and a refined dining experience. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular spot for fresh tuna; long lines but worth it for the freshness. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Shinjuku | Known for its creative rolls and excellent service; great value for the quality. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Roppongi | Small, family‑run shop; offers a more casual yet authentic sushi experience. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic sushi experience; well‑known for its consistency and high standards. |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Chuo | Offers a wide variety of nigiri and sashimi; praised for its friendly atmosphere. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Marunouchi | Known for its traditional Edomae style and meticulous presentation. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Minato | Three Michelin stars; renowned for its precision and use of premium fish. |

These spots range from ultra‑high‑end Michelin‑starred experiences to more accessible, bustling market stalls. If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations well in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred places—and be prepared for potentially long wait times at the popular market locations. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
